createdBy: codex gpt-5.6-sol via T-011 re-plan review rev3 (00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000), finding 2
impact:
## The contradiction

T-011 AC 10 reads: "`spendbar refresh` reaches the running service over the socket and **triggers a refresh**; with no service running it fails with a clear, typed message."

The base plan's accepted reduction (§10.1) is that **T-011 alone indexes once**: every generation it publishes carries `sourceVersion = {}`, so no later candidate can dominate and no second publish is possible. Review of the re-plan established that the honest response to a post-bootstrap refresh is to decline it at ADMISSION, before spawning ccusage at all — spending 60-120 seconds on a run that is known in advance to be incapable of publishing is worse than declining, and it makes a healthy service indistinguishable from a broken one.

So after the bootstrap publish, no refresh is triggered. The command reaches the service and receives a typed terminal outcome. AC 10 as written is not satisfiable.

## Why this needs an owner ruling rather than a planner's reading

Two readings are defensible and they lead to different tickets:

- **AC 10 means "the command reaches the service and gets a truthful typed answer".** Then it is dischargeable in two halves: before the bootstrap publish it triggers a real refresh; after, it returns the typed decline. AC 10 is amended to say so explicitly, and T-011 proceeds.
- **AC 10 means "a refresh actually executes on every invocation".** Then it is not satisfiable in v0.2 at all and T-011 is held on ISS-082 then ISS-081 along with everything else that needs the watermark contract.

The first reading was assumed by revision 2 of the re-plan without being stated, and that was wrong. It is recorded here rather than reinterpreted quietly.

## Related design consequence, whichever way it goes

If the first reading is adopted, the decline must be surfaced rather than reported as success or as a generic failure: a `refreshMode` capability on `status`, a typed terminal outcome distinct from both "nothing changed" and "failed", a distinct non-zero exit code with a message naming the limitation, a terminal progress frame that is not a fabricated completion, and a log line at the admission decision. Reporting "cannot look" as "looked, nothing moved" is the freshness lie N-008 1b exists to prevent.
resolution:
RESOLVED by N-009 plus an AC rewording on 2026-08-04.

The issue was correct at the time: AC 10 required `spendbar refresh` to "trigger a refresh", and under the v0.2 indexes-once reduction the service published one bootstrap generation and never indexed again, so there was nothing for a refresh to trigger. The AC could not be discharged.

WHAT CHANGED. The indexes-once reduction was not a design preference — it existed ONLY because no truthful `sourceVersion` was definable (ISS-075, then ISS-081/ISS-082: the key domain was undefined and no per-source sub-day time existed). N-009 (docs/snapshot-facts-and-watermarks.md v2) defines it: six ingestion surfaces as the key domain, per-surface watermarks attesting recency, and separate coverage attestation, with four publish outcomes including `refreshed` for the equal-watermark-with-content-update case. Repeated publishing is therefore meaningful again, and the reduction that made AC 10 vacuous is superseded.

WHAT WAS REWORDED, AND WHY IT IS NOT A WEAKENING. AC 10 now reads: `spendbar refresh` reaches the running service over the socket and the service ENQUEUES AND RUNS a refresh job; with no service running it fails with a clear, typed message. Whether that job's publish yields a new generation, `unchanged`, or a typed refusal is the STORE's verdict.

That split is the honest one under RULES.md L-006. T-011 owns the mechanism — the socket path, the queue, job admission and execution — and can witness every part of it. It does not own and cannot witness the publish verdict: this ticket does not compute `sourceVersion` at all, it submits a candidate and takes the answer. Assigning the publish outcome to T-011's AC would be requiring a premise this ticket's caller cannot supply, which is the exact failure L-006 was adopted to stop.

DEPENDENCY RECORDED: T-025 is now listed as a SOFT dependency on T-011. T-025 implements N-009's registry, watermarks and coverage and is currently parked on ISS-090/ISS-091. T-011 does not need it to build the queue, socket, launcher or lifecycle — but any claim about repeated publishing is contingent on it, and that contingency is written into the ticket rather than left to be discovered.

This was park reason 2 for T-011. It no longer is.
title: T-011 AC 10 requires that `spendbar refresh` "triggers a refresh", which the v0.2 indexes-once reduction cannot satisfy after the bootstrap publish
